description: wake.log grows unbounded. Every wake appends to $DIR/state/wake.log (founder-loop.sh:24) with no rotation, truncation, or size cap. Under a cron/launchd cadence (the intended deployment, spec line 96) this file grows without bound and will eventually consume disk. This is NOT a blocker against the core question: it CANNOT fabricate or inflate an earning (the goal-check reads the ledger, not wake.log), CANNOT corrupt STATE (atomic tmp+mv is independent of wake.log), CANNOT mislead the goal-check, and requires NO human. It is a pure operability/disk-hygiene concern, hence advisory only.
fix: Add log rotation/capping, e.g. before the append: keep only the last N lines (`tail -n 5000 "$DIR/state/wake.log" > "$DIR/state/wake.log.tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv ...`), or rely on an external logrotate entry in the cadence. Non-blocking; track for G1.1-B hardening.
